items.description: 19 of the 20 spec deltas (every change except toolkit-consistency) are plan-roadmap scaffolds whose scenarios are circular: `WHEN <change-id> is implemented THEN <acceptance outcome>`. Each SHALL technically has a WHEN/THEN, but none is verifiable, and all sit under the placeholder capability `multiplayer-collaboration`, for which no `openspec/specs/` directory exists. toolkit-consistency's own plan-findings graded this same pattern 'critical testability' and replaced it. Acceptable as scaffolds that /plan-feature or PLAN_ITERATE must refine, but they must not pass through to IMPLEMENT as-is.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: The scaffold generator truncates requirement headings mid-sentence with `...` and lowercases the first character of the outcome, producing `pRs created by` here (and `that given any`, `that /implement-feature` elsewhere). `### Requirement:` headings are the identity used by opsx:sync and by the planned requirement-level collision scanner (ri-06), so truncated, near-identical headings undermine the very collision detection this roadmap introduces.

items.description: The rationale for `proposal_approval: auto` is that a recorded `roadmap_approval` already authorizes the plans inside a roadmap. But `proposal_approval` also fires for standalone changes started via /plan-feature or /autopilot with no parent roadmap, where no roadmap_approval exists. As written, the posture removes the only human intent gate for non-roadmap changes, which contradicts the epic's own P3 (intent is an owned artifact) and the fail-closed constraint.

items.description: The One-way consumption requirement says merged shared records 'SHALL participate in the existing deduplication', and design.md states that dedupe key is `(capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id)`. But the Exported learning privacy requirement drops `session_id` and allowlists only `event_type, summary, outcome, lessons, tags, created_at`, so neither `session_id` nor top-level `capability_gap`/`affected_skill` exist on an exported record. The exporter's own dedupe key `(capability_gap, affected_skill, summary)` likewise uses two fields that are not in the allowlist. The two requirements cannot both hold unless capability_gap/affected_skill are recovered from tags and the consumer dedupe key is changed.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md Exported learning privacy names capability_gap/affected_skill as retained tag values; One-way consumption dedupes shared records on (capability_gap, affected_skill, summary).

items.description: The privacy requirement drops the `agent_id` and `session_id` fields but exports `tags` verbatim. Per docs/guides/memory-conventions.md, memory entries are tagged with identifiers such as `agent:<id>`, `session:<id>`, `change:<id>` and vendor/model tags, so the identity the allowlist removes re-enters through tags. The secret sanitizer targets credential patterns, not identifiers, so it will not catch this. No scenario covers tag-encoded identity.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md tags filtered to D4 namespaces; identity/context tags dropped; scenario 'Identity-bearing tags are dropped' added.

items.description: Because the stamp is the pin (D3) and every successful install overwrites it, a teammate who runs install.sh from an un-pinned toolkit checkout silently moves the team's pin instead of hitting drift. The drift check only runs under `--check`. No scenario covers 'install over an existing stamp whose hash differs from the new source', so the implementation is free to overwrite without even a notice; the only safeguard is a git diff on a hash string.

items.description: Runtime drift hashes each installed mirror with the *source checkout's* manifest (`$INSTALL_MANIFEST`), not the mirror's own `install-manifest.json`. The pinned `payload_hash` was computed over the pinned manifest's skill set. Whenever the checkout's portable skill set differs from the pinned one (a skill removed, renamed, or flipped portable→non-portable between commit A and commit B), a mirror that is byte-identical to the pinned payload hashes differently and `--check` prints 'Runtime drift ... Re-run install.sh from the pinned toolkit commit' in addition to checkout drift. The spec's Checkout drift scenario expects only the checkout-drift message, and the runtime-drift remediation text is wrong in that case (re-running from the pinned commit changes nothing). Session-log decision 6 chose this to also catch a missing skill, but mirror parity already reports that. Fix: hash the mirror with its own manifest (omit `--manifest` or pass `$TARGET_ROOT/$rel_dir/install-manifest.json`); `test_checkout_drift` should add a skill removal in checkout B to pin the behaviour.
items.resolution: IMPL_FIX 1 (000c2bc): check_install_stamp hashes each mirror against its own synced install-manifest.json; test_checkout_drift_with_changed_skill_set_is_not_runtime_drift

items.description: Re-verified ledger 10: still open. `write_install_stamp` never reads the existing stamp, so an install from any checkout silently replaces the pin with no notice when the new `payload_hash` differs from the committed one; the only signal remains the git diff of a hash string. No scenario or test covers 'install over an existing stamp with a different hash'. Remains deferred per plan-findings; a one-line 'Pin moved: <old prefix> -> <new prefix>' notice would close it cheaply.
items.resolution: echo of ledger 10 (re-verification landed as a new item); ledger 10 stays open advisory, deferred per plan-findings

items.description: `load_shared_learnings` documents that unreadable files are skipped with a warning because the projection is advisory, but it only catches `OSError`. A `learnings.jsonl` with invalid UTF-8 raises `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`) and aborts the whole analysis. Likewise `sharing_enabled()` imports the sibling exporter unconditionally, so a mirror missing `export_shared_learnings.py` raises `ImportError` for every user, including those who never opted in. Catch `ValueError` on the read and guard the import so an optional feature cannot fail the core pipeline.

After `merge_shared_learnings`, the merged list goes through `rank_findings`, whose grouping key is `(capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id)`. Exported records carry no `session_id`, so every shared record for the same gap+skill (different summaries, from many teammate sessions) collapses into one occurrence while the same signals locally would count once per session. Shared learnings therefore systematically undercount frequency relative to local ones. Acceptable for an advisory projection, but worth a sentence in SKILL.md or a synthetic per-record key for shared entries.

`rank_findings` now emits `origin:<value>` strings into `sources` for any entry carrying an `origin:` tag, not only shared records. `sources` previously held bare `source:` values (e.g. `self-reported`); consumers such as `generate_report.py` that render or map source labels will see a new value shape. Silent change to an existing public return shape; document it or namespace it in a separate field.

The stamp records `agents` but `check_install_stamp` never reads it: runtime drift iterates the CLI `agent_list` (default `claude,agents`). A consumer that installed with `--agents claude` and later runs a bare `--check` gets failures for a mirror that was never meant to exist, and the stamp's `agents` field has no consumer at all. Either drive the runtime-drift loop from the stamp's `agents`, or document that `--check` must be invoked with the same `--agents` as the install.

The new 'Shared Learnings' section says consumption happens in `analyze_failures.py`, but session-log Implementation 1 decision 12 records that `generate_report.py` runs its own `query_memory` + `rank_findings` pipeline and does not merge the shared file. If the skill's report workflow goes through `generate_report.py`, enabling sharing changes nothing a user sees, and SKILL.md does not state this fallback. Either state the limitation under Consumption or route `generate_report.py` through `load_shared_learnings`/`merge_shared_learnings` (follow-up change).

The Verification command runs `install.sh` against this repository, which is a self-install: by design it writes no stamp and `--check` skips the stamp comparison, so this line cannot verify T2/T3 at all. T7 was actually verified against a scratch consumer (session-log Implementation 2). Replace with the scratch-consumer form (`--target <scratch>`) or note that the self-install run only covers mirror parity.

Exclusion is applied after `rglob` has already descended into the excluded tree, so a skill containing `node_modules/` or large `tests/` fixtures is fully stat-walked three times per `--check` (source plus two mirrors). `os.walk` with in-place pruning of `dirnames` skips those subtrees entirely and keeps the same ordering guarantee after sorting.

The docstring claims symlinks are followed, but `Path.rglob` does not descend into symlinked *subdirectories* (pathlib skips `entry.is_symlink()` directories during `**` recursion in every supported Python version). Top-level skill-dir symlinks work (the start directory is opened directly), which is why `test_symlinked_tree_hashes_identically` passes, but a symlinked directory nested inside a skill is silently omitted from the hash. Also `payload_names` only catches `(OSError, ValueError, KeyError)`; a manifest whose top level is a list or whose `skills` values are not objects raises `TypeError`/`AttributeError` as a traceback instead of the documented exit 2. Narrow the docstring claim (or use `os.walk(followlinks=True)`) and widen the except.

Two SHALL clauses lack a verifying scenario: Payload hash's 'following symlinks' (a `--mode symlink` mirror hashing identically; the test exists but the spec has no scenario), and the 'Projection never feeds canonical state' scenario under State-artifact registration is a restated constraint with no observable WHEN/THEN (what fails if a skill does derive state from it?). Add a symlink-mode scenario under Payload hash and either drop the second scenario or tie it to a concrete check (e.g. the guard test asserting the state-artifacts row text, which is what the implementation actually verifies).

`phase_history` is not chronological: PLAN_REVIEW `converged` is stamped 2026-10-09T12:19:10Z, followed by two PLAN_FIX sub-steps at 08:25 and 08:31 and a `degraded` PLAN_REVIEW entry at 12:20. plan-findings.md dates the same convergence 08:21Z/08:30Z. The cherry-picked sub-step records carry the sub-agent's clock while the orchestrator entries carry its own, so a reader reconstructing the phase timeline from the canonical file gets contradictory ordering. Orchestrator-owned; distinct from ledger 15 (stale escalation fields).

The exporter applies no gap filter of its own: whatever `query_memory` returns is projected, and an entry without `capability_gap:`/`failure_type:` tags is exported with dedupe key `(unknown, unknown, summary)`. The privacy posture therefore depends on `query_memory`'s server-side tag filter staying narrow; if that query is ever widened (e.g. to decisions or handoff summaries), non-gap episodic text lands in a tracked, shared file. A defensive `if not any(t.startswith(('capability_gap:', 'failure_type:')) ...): continue` keeps the exporter's contract independent of upstream. Relatedly, `load_sanitizer()` raises an uncaught `FileNotFoundError` traceback when `session-log` is not co-installed instead of a documented refusal.

`test_aborted_install_leaves_previous_stamp_intact` compares bytes, but the only field that would differ on an erroneous rewrite is `installed_at` at one-second resolution (same payload, agents and mode). If the stamp were wrongly written before `check_openspec_cli` and both writes fell in the same UTC second, the test passes against the broken ordering. Mutate the prior stamp first (e.g. add a `"marker": 1` key or change `installed_at`) so any rewrite is detected deterministically.
items.resolution: IMPL_FIX 2 (000c2bc): test_aborted_install_leaves_previous_stamp_intact marks the prior stamp so any rewrite is byte-detectable

items.description: When the user passes `--shared-learnings <path>` explicitly but `config.json` does not enable sharing, the file is ignored with no message. The behaviour is correct per spec, but an explicit flag silently doing nothing is hard to diagnose; a one-line stderr notice ('shared learnings ignored: sharing not enabled in <config>') would make the opt-in rule discoverable.

The runtime-drift loop now depends on `$TARGET_ROOT/$rel_dir/install-manifest.json` existing in every mirror. When it does not (a mirror synced by a pre-manifest install.sh, a mirror whose manifest was deleted, or, per open ledger 40, an agent in the CLI `agent_list` that was never installed), payload_hash.py exits 2 and the only output is the generic 'Cannot compute mirror payload hash for <agent>'. That is a legitimate drift condition (mirror no longer matches the pinned payload) but it is neither the spec's runtime-drift message naming the pinned `toolkit_version`/`source_commit` nor a hint about the missing manifest. Before invoking the helper, test for the mirror manifest: if absent, print the runtime-drift message with a 'mirror manifest missing' qualifier (and skip the agent entirely when it is not listed in the stamp's `agents`, which also closes ledger 40).

The new test correctly fails against the pre-fix code (checkout B's manifest drops json-canvas, so the mirror hash no longer equals the stamp and 'Runtime drift' is printed). But its negative assertions are loose: if install.sh stopped syncing `install-manifest.json` into the mirrors, payload_hash.py would exit 2, stderr would read 'Cannot compute mirror payload hash', the exit code would still be 1 and 'Checkout drift' would still be present, so the test would pass while the feature it pins is broken. Add `assert "Cannot compute" not in result.stderr` (or assert the exact expected stderr lines) so the test only passes on the intended path. Also note the hard-coded dependency on `json-canvas` being portable in the real manifest; the explicit `assert manifest["skills"]["json-canvas"] == ...` makes that coupling fail loudly, which is acceptable, but picking the first portable skill from the manifest would make the test independent of that skill's future scoping.
items.resolution: IMPL_FIX 3 (2cf3614): test asserts 'Cannot compute mirror payload hash' is absent, so a missing mirror manifest cannot mask the runtime-drift path

items.description: Fourteen pre-existing ledger entries change only in the relative order of `resolution`, `parked_reason` and `consensus_status`, with identical values. The ledger writer serialises keys in insertion order rather than a stable order, so every round that touches an entry re-emits unrelated entries and inflates the diff reviewers must read. The substantive additions (35 and 48 addressed with the 000c2bc reference, 36 retired as an echo of 10, 37-47 and 49 opened) are correct and consistent with the spec; the open items listed for re-verification are untouched by this diff and remain open. Consider `json.dump(..., sort_keys=True)` or a fixed key order in the ledger writer so future rounds diff only what changed.
